slides.title: The 90/180 rule: when can you go back?
slides.body: It applies to everyone visiting Schengen visa-free or on a short-stay visa.

slides.title: At most 90 days in any 180
slides.body: The 180 days are not a fixed calendar period. The window moves every day: count back 180 days from today and add up the days you spent in Schengen.

slides.title: Entry and exit days count as full days
slides.body: A day you arrive in the morning and leave in the evening is still one day. The UK and Ireland are not in Schengen, so days there don't count.

slides.title: 1 June to 29 August 2026
slides.body: That is all 90 days. The first day you can enter again is 28 November 2026, when 1 June drops out of the 180-day window.

slides.title: Try it with your own dates
slides.body: Enter your trips to see how many days you have left and when you can return. You can share the result as a link.

caption:
The Schengen 90/180 rule: you can stay at most 90 days in any 180-day period. The window moves every day, and entry and exit days count as full days.

Example: if you stayed from 1 June to 29 August 2026, you have used all 90 days. The first day you can enter again is 28 November 2026.

Check your own dates: travelnow.info/schengen-calculator/ (link in bio)

Source: EU Regulation 2018/1806
